meta.temperature_K_convention: Pair is [min_K, max_K]. Use null for max to mean no upper bound. A number always means that number — there is no magic threshold. (999 is still read as no-bound for older files, but is deprecated: write null.)

general.description: Unicellular extremophiles capable of surviving across extreme temperatures, chemical environments, and atmospheres. They derive energy from photosynthetic, chemosynthetic, or thermosynthetic processes and often coexist with other lifeforms.

species.description: Neon-atmosphere bacteria forming bright looping whirls.
species._atmosphereNote: Neon here means neon air, not the word Neon in the label. All 213 observed acies bodies are 85.36-100% neon, and the 'NeonRich' worlds the row also matched average 5.5% neon - nitrogen with a neon trace, which is where Fonticulua segmentatus lives (0.24-0.53% neon on all 16 of its bodies). The floor is 50% because that is where the game itself stops calling a body Neon: across 8,000 journal scans, plain Neon runs 50.29-100% and NeonRich never exceeds 49.74%. A demotion, not a wall. This also closes the 93% helium / 6.7% neon body that passed the 5% required-gas floor. See tests/atmosphereGasShare.test.ts.

species.description: Sunlight-dependent ammonia bacteria forming maze-like colonies.
species._colourNote: The mapping used to be the sentence 'Parent star type determines color', which is prose and not a table, so colourFromStar iterated the string's character indices and matched nothing: alcyoneum reported no colour on every body it has ever grown on. The table is the one it shares with cerbrus and aurasus, confirmed against 11 of the commander's own sightings where the host star resolves to one class. See tests/bacteriumColourTables.test.ts.

species.description: Methane-based bacteria forming linked bubble-like structures.
Water/sulfur dioxide bacteria forming brain-like clusters.
Thermosynthetic bacteria linked to nitrogen/ammonia volcanism.
species._atmosphereNote: Neon was a wall here and the corpus does not support one: 45% Thin Neon, 32% Neon-rich, and the rest Argon, Water-rich, Methane and airless. The commander sampled it on Thin Methane at Synookooe WW-F b55-0 A 2 a, a moon whose sibling one orbit out — same class, same Thin Methane, no volcanism — carried Bacterium bullaris instead. The volcanism is the real rule: 95.5% of its 22 observed bodies have nitrogen or ammonia volcanism against 4.4% ambient in the population it lives in, an enrichment of 21.8x. See tests/volcanismBacteriumGates.test.ts.

Neon was a wall here and the corpus does not support one: 59% Thin Neon, 24% Thin Argon, which the row never listed. The volcanism is the real rule: every one of its 17 observed bodies has carbon or methane volcanism, against 2.5% ambient — an enrichment of 40.7x. See tests/volcanismBacteriumGates.test.ts.

species.description: Web-like bacteria. Grows where there is volcanism, or where the surface reaches 300 K.
species._presenceNote: Volcanism, or 300 K, and nothing else gates it. Corpus: 687 of 687 tela bodies satisfy 'volcanic OR T>=300' and 0 of 10,630 cold non-volcanic Bacterium bodies carry it. Independent EDDN/journal sample: 33 of 33. Canonn Bioforge, 46,123 sightings over six colours: 60-66% at T>=300 K and 66-67% with no volcanism, the two shares matching per colour. On hot bodies it is a coin flip against cerbrus (570 vs 589) and no discriminator exists - both are listed. See docs/tela-decision-20092026.md and docs/tela-verification-20092026-opus.md.

species.description: Volcanic bacteria associated with water-based activity.
species._atmosphereNote: Neon was a wall here and it is not even this species' commonest atmosphere: Thin Argon 38% against Thin Neon 35%, and Argon was never in the list. The volcanism is the real rule: every one of its 26 observed bodies has water volcanism, against 2.3% ambient — an enrichment of 44.1x. See tests/volcanismBacteriumGates.test.ts.

species.description: Argon-based bacteria forming tight loop clusters.
species._atmosphereNote: Argon-dominant. 880 of its 881 observed bodies are plain Thin Argon at 51.6-100% argon and not one is Thin Argon-rich, where argon averages 3% and the air is usually nitrogen. Argon-rich is 2.9% of argon habitats in the corpus, so 0 of 880 is a distribution and not a thin sample: under indifference that outcome has probability 6e-12. Without the band the required-gas floor of 5% lets vesicula through on an Argon-rich body carrying 30% argon - one of Fonticulua upupam's worlds. Same evidence as Fonticulua campestris at a larger n. See tests/atmosphereGasShare.test.ts.

species.description: Carbon dioxide atmosphere bacteria forming radial streak patterns.
species._colourNote: Aurasus is coloured by its parent star, not by the ground. The material table this row used to carry scored 4 of 15 against the commander's own sightings, and all four were 'Green', which sits in both tables by coincidence; the star table scores 15 of 15, with 11 of those on bodies whose host star resolves to a single class. His own photographs agree - Emerald, Green, Lime and Teal are G, K, F and M, and not one of them appears in the material table. Because the predicted colour also chooses the photograph, the app could almost never show the right picture for the commonest Bacterium in the corpus. Table from https://ed-dsn.net/en/bacterium_en/, same as alcyoneum and cerbrus. See tests/bacteriumColourTables.test.ts.

species.description: Oxygen-based bacteria forming swirling surface patterns.

volcanism_dependencies._retired: Not a requirement — 706 of 833 observed bodies have no volcanism. Kept here as the note it always was; nothing reads this block.

special_rules: ALL species require a thin atmosphere (hard requirement)
Atmosphere type is the PRIMARY filter for species selection
Some species require BOTH atmosphere AND volcanism (critical edge case)
Color variation is either material-based OR star-based depending on species
Largest and most complex genus so far (multi-layer condition system)
